title: Philadelphia Fed First Quarter 2027 Survey of Professional Forecasters — 10:00 a.m. ET, the date re-derived from a one-step release rule that is 16 for 16 where the inherited two-step rule was 8 of 13
source: EST: DERIVED, not read — no primary source for this date exists yet, and that is stated rather than papered over. The Philadelphia Fed's calendar endpoint (philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200, 130,695 bytes) still enumerates 2026 only: four SPF rows, 'First Quarter 2026' through 'Fourth Quarter 2026 | Nov 16 2026 | 10:00 a.m.', and zero 2027 rows anywhere in the payload — unchanged from the 2026-09-09 fetch that produced the proposal this file supersedes. THE DATE IS NOW DERIVED FROM A DIFFERENT AND STRONGER RULE THAN THE PROPOSAL'S. The proposal chained two inferences: deadline = second Tuesday of the middle month, then release = +3 business days excluding weekends and federal holidays. Re-run out-of-sample against Q1 only, from the publisher's own spf-release-dates.txt (re-fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200, 8,298 bytes, byte-identical to the 2026-09-09 pull, 146 quarters parsed since 1990Q2), that chain reproduces just 8 of 13 non-shutdown Q1 release dates since 2012 and 11 of 36 across the full history — it misses 2013, 2014, 2020, 2022 and 2025 outright, because the deadline is the Tuesday of the month's second CALENDAR week, which is the FIRST Tuesday of February in years when Feb 1 falls Wednesday or later. THE ONE-STEP REPLACEMENT skips the deadline entirely: the Q1 release is THE FRIDAY BETWEEN FEBRUARY 9 AND 15 INCLUSIVE (exactly one such Friday exists per year) — 16 of 16 non-shutdown Q1 releases since 2009, 13 of 13 since 2012, zero exceptions; and the weaker day-of-month band alone (Feb 9-15, any weekday) holds 20 of 20 since 2005. The Friday in the 2027 window is Fri 2027-02-12. BOTH RULES AGREE ON 2027-02-12, so the proposal's date survives on stronger evidence than it was filed with. Q1 is also the structurally cleanest quarter for a release rule: Presidents Day is the third Monday of February and therefore never falls before February 15, so no federal holiday can ever land inside a Tuesday-to-Friday Q1 window — which is why Q1 is 13 of 13 Fridays while Q4, where Veterans Day sits inside the window, is only 4 of 13. Presidents Day 2027 is Mon 2027-02-15, three days AFTER this release. Filed estimate on the strongest possible grounds for that label: no page anywhere states this date, market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's release schedule, and this lane never self-confirms. Checked 2026-09-10
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-10 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/survey-of-professional-forecasters-q1-2027-02-12.from-survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16.json, filed 2026-09-09) and discharged the three tasks it assigned. THE PROPOSAL ASKED TO BE FALSIFIED AND WAS, IN PART: its date stands, its rule does not. See `source` — the inherited deadline-plus-business-days chain is 8 of 13 on Q1 since 2012; the one-step 'Friday between February 9 and 15' rule is 16 of 16 since 2009. The two agree for 2027 only because Feb 1 2027 is a Monday, the one weekday alignment where the second-Tuesday and second-calendar-week readings coincide. A lane dating a FUTURE SPF edition should use the one-step rule and should NOT carry the proposal's rule forward. IMPACT LOW AND SYMBOLS [] ARE RE-MEASURED, NOT INHERITED, AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT CORRECTS THE SIBLING LEDGER'S EMPHASIS. Pooled across 145 releases the null holds, as survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16 found. But sliced by quarter it scatters in both directions: release-day vs non-release-day mean absolute close-to-close ratios are, for the 10-year breakeven T10YIE, Q1 1.00 / Q2 1.32 / Q3 0.85 / Q4 0.70; for VIX, Q1 1.26 / Q2 0.90 / Q3 0.82 / Q4 1.15; for the 10-year note DGS10, Q1 1.24 / Q2 1.02 / Q3 1.00 / Q4 0.84. Twelve subsamples, ratios from 0.70 to 1.32, and the single largest Welch t is -2.47 — NEGATIVE, on Q4's breakeven. That is what a null looks like when it is sliced twelve ways, and it means the sibling's '23 for 23 at or under 5bp' November result and this session's Q1 elevation are the same artifact pointing opposite directions. NEITHER SHOULD BE QUOTED AS A PROPERTY OF A QUARTER. Attribution supports that reading: the three largest Q1 release-day VIX moves are 2026-03-06 (the shutdown-delayed release, 5.74), 2018-02-09 (4.40, inside the Volmageddon week) and 2022-02-11 (3.45, the Ukraine-invasion warning); drop those three and the Q1 VIX ratio falls from 1.26 to 0.96. DGS10 does not collapse the same way — it stays at 1.25 on the remaining 33 days — and that is recorded as an unexplained residual rather than argued away. SHUTDOWN DELAY IS A Q1 RISK SPECIFICALLY, WHICH IS THIS ENTRY'S LOAD-BEARING FACT. The publisher's own footnotes name four shutdown-delayed surveys — 2026Q1, 2019Q1, 2013Q4 and 1996Q1 — and THREE OF THE FOUR ARE Q1s: 3 of 36 Q1s (8.3%) against 1 of 110 other quarters (0.9%). The mechanism is that federal funding lapses cluster in the October-to-January window and the Q1 survey's jump-off values are exactly the statistics those agencies stop producing. The precedent is dated and recent: the 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-12 shutdown ended in November and the 2026Q1 survey STILL slipped from a rule-implied 2026-02-13 to an actual 2026-03-06, a 21-day delay. This calendar tracks cr-expiry-2026-12-11 and government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11 (both high, both estimate) 63 days before this print, and that is the single channel by which 2027-02-12 realistically moves. SCHEDULING: 2027-02-12 carries no other tracked event, canonical or proposed — the same clean-tape property the Q4 edition had. The derived collection deadline Tue 2027-02-09 is NOT CPI day, unlike Q4's, because this calendar tracks no 2027 CPI at all (the cpi-* series stops at cpi-2026-12-10); bls.gov returned 403 to this session, so no 2027 CPI date is proposed here rather than guessed. Corridor: 7 days after jobs-2027-02-05 (high, estimate), 3 days before presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15, 5 days before the proposed fomc-minutes-2027-02-17. This is an ESTIMATE and a LOW: it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
